proposed_comments.title: Preserve unavailable response time (1/5)
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve unavailable response time (1/5)

**Severity:** `medium`

The average-response-time counter is optional, so the model should preserve an unavailable reading rather than represent it as a measurement. Making this property nullable lets the card omit the value until a finite sample has been accepted.

```suggestion
        public float? ResponseTime
```

confidence.rationale: The pinned source path from the optional counter through Math.Max to formatting is grounded, and the deterministic candidate regression tests cover non-finite values. Physical counter behavior remains unverified.

proposed_comments.title: Filter non-finite samples at the source (2/5)
proposed_comments.body:
### Filter non-finite samples at the source (2/5)

**Severity:** `medium`

A counter can be present and still return a non-finite value; Math.Max does not filter NaN. Apply the finite-value helper before storing the sample so invalid readings remain unavailable.

```suggestion
                    DiskUsages[name].ResponseTime = GetResponseTime(diskCounterWithName.Value[3].NextValue());
```

confidence.rationale: The pinned source path from the optional counter through Math.Max to formatting is grounded, and the deterministic candidate regression tests cover non-finite values. Physical counter behavior remains unverified.

proposed_comments.title: Normalize only finite response times (3/5)
proposed_comments.body:
### Normalize only finite response times (3/5)

**Severity:** `medium`

Keep response-time normalization at one boundary: return null for NaN or either infinity, and preserve the non-negative clamp for finite readings. Otherwise an invalid value can flow through to display as NaN ms.

```suggestion
        hasPreviousSample && float.IsFinite(idlePercent) ? Math.Clamp(100f - idlePercent, 0f, 100f) : 0f;

    internal static float? GetResponseTime(float seconds) =>
        float.IsFinite(seconds) ? Math.Max(0f, seconds) : null;
```

confidence.rationale: The pinned source path from the optional counter through Math.Max to formatting is grounded, and the deterministic candidate regression tests cover non-finite values. Physical counter behavior remains unverified.
